referenceOrigin: Exact arcade and printer entries from the approved studio.json atlas, arranged in two rows of four copies at 10x nearest-neighbor scale on a 1536x1024 transparent canvas.
prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: production pixel-art prop animation sheet for the existing Agent Office room. Edit the supplied 1536x1024 transparent reference sheet in place. Keep exactly two rows and four equal columns, eight whole sprites total. Top row is the same red-trimmed navy arcade cabinet in every frame; bottom row is the same grey printer on its brown wooden stand in every frame. Preserve the exact reference viewpoint, silhouette, cabinet/stand dimensions, position within each slot, chunky low-resolution pixel clusters, navy outlines, warm cream highlights and limited color palette. No new furniture. Do not add characters, text, labels, borders, scenery, floor, shadows or backgrounds. Actual transparent alpha around each separate sprite, with generous empty horizontal and vertical gaps. All sprites fully visible. Top-row four-frame looping animation: tiny green arcade invader advances horizontally across the screen and returns, with a restrained screen glow; the cabinet, control panel, red trim and base remain still. Bottom-row four-frame looping animation: cream paper advances slightly out of the existing printer slot and retracts, with one tiny green activity light change; the printer housing and wooden stand remain still. Keep frame 1 of each row identical to the supplied idle pose. Keep exact same object scale, facing direction and bottom-center anchor in all four columns. Crisp nearest-neighbor pixel art, no antialiasing or gradients. This is a whole sprite-strip edit, not a poster or concept illustration. Preserve the source canvas dimensions.
normalization: The unmodified output is preserved. The environment compiler uses one shared source crop and scale per object, bottom-centers on the seed footprint, maps RGB to the seed palette and thresholds alpha at 224 for crisp pixels. Frame zero is locked to the exact shipped seed. Reviewed screen/paper/light regions receive generated pixels; the cabinet and stand outside those regions remain pixel-identical to the seed in every frame. Reviewed regions, crops, anchors, scales, source and native pixel hashes are in prop-life.json beside the compiled atlas.
